Mode.Name: Complexity
Mode.Hint: How much rules weight a trade carries. Each feature can still be turned on or off on its own.

Tables.Name: Price tables
Tables.Hint: Prices, rates and rounding steps that differ from the defaults.

Proximity.Name: Trade only up close
Proximity.Hint: Players must have their own token within 2 squares of the merchant's token to trade. The GM can always trade.

Compendiums.Name: Stock compendiums
Compendiums.Hint: Item compendiums the stock generator draws from. Leave empty to use dnd5e's own equipment for the world's rules.

RestockDays.Name: Restock every
RestockDays.Hint: In-game days between automatic restocks of every shop. 0 turns automatic restocks off.

AttitudeScope.Name: Attitude is kept
AttitudeScope.Hint: Each merchant remembers every character on their own, or the whole party as one.

AttitudeDecay.Name: Attitude fades
AttitudeDecay.Hint: Each full in-game week, every merchant's attitude moves 1 point back toward neutral.

Reactions.Name: Merchant reactions
Reactions.Hint: A short line under the merchant's portrait reacts to the offer. Archetypes can have their own lines.

Greeting.Name: Merchant greetings
Greeting.Hint: A merchant greets a player in a speech bubble when their token comes close. Needs core chat bubbles.

SoundVolume.Name: Coin sounds
SoundVolume.Hint: How loud coins sound when you put something on offer and when a trade is done, on top of your interface volume. 0 turns them off. Only for you.

CoinBurst.Name: Coin burst
CoinBurst.Hint: Coins spray from the merchant's token when a trade is done. Uses core's new particle effects, which may change in later Foundry versions. Only for you.

TheftApproval.Name: Thefts need GM approval
TheftApproval.Hint: When theft is on, a theft can wait for you to allow it before the player rolls.

Error.NoGM: A GM must be online to trade.
Error.NoAnswer: The GM did not answer. Try again.
Error.Busy: Busy with {name}. Try again when they are done.
Error.NotYours: You can only trade as a character you own.
Error.NoCharacter: You have no character to trade with.
Error.ExactCoins: {name} can't make change. Pay with exact coins.
Error.TradeFailed: The trade could not be completed. Nothing changed.
Error.NeedsApproval: This shop needs the GM to approve each trade.
Error.GMOnly: Only a GM can do that.
Error.ProposalGone: This proposal has already been answered.
Error.RevertGone: That trade is not in the ledger, or was already reverted.
Error.RevertMoved: {name} has changed hands since the trade, so it can't be reverted.
Error.RevertCoins: The coins from that trade have been spent, so it can't be reverted.
Error.SoldOut: That item is no longer available.
Error.NoRoll: The roll did not reach the GM. Try again.
Error.PlayersOnly: Player trades are between two players' characters.
Error.OwnBoth: You play {name} too. Move items between their sheets instead.
Error.OfferChanged: The offer changed. Check it and accept again.
Error.JoinGM: A GM can't join a trade. Trade as a character instead.
Error.NothingToJoin: Nobody is trading with {name} right now.
Error.NotJoined: That character is not part of this trade anymore.
Error.NoService: This merchant does not offer that service.
Error.RevertService: Trades with a service can't be reverted. Undo them by hand.

Configure.Title: Shop: {name}

Open.Label: Open
Open.Hint: Players can trade here only while the shop is open.

Remote.Label: Trade from the Shops list
Remote.Hint: Once the party has visited, players can trade here from the Shops list in the token controls, without walking up.

TheftProof.Label: Theft-proof
TheftProof.Hint: Nobody can try to steal here, such as at a temple, a vault or a guarded shop.

ExecutionMode.Label: Trades
ExecutionMode.Hint: Instant trades go through as soon as the offer balances. With GM approval, you approve, counter or decline each one.

Stock.Hint: Loose items are the stock. Equipped gear stays with the merchant. Leave a price empty to sell at the item's value. Pin an item to keep it through restocks. Drop items, a folder or a roll table here to add stock.
Stock.Empty: This actor has no items to sell. Drop items onto its sheet to stock the shelf.

Configure.GenerateConfirm: This replaces {count} unpinned items on the shelf. Pinned items stay.
Configure.ArchetypeHint: The kind of shop. It decides what stock rolls and which trade-ins it pays more for.
Configure.TierHint: How many items it stocks, how rare they get, and how much coin is in its purse.
Configure.PostCardHint: Posts a chat card with a Trade button for everyone.
Configure.RemoveBody: {name} goes back to being a normal NPC, and players can no longer trade here. Its items stay where they are.
Configure.RemoveForgetHint: Clears shelf prices, pins, attitude, the ledger, visits and the Wanted board. Leave it unticked to get them back if you turn the shop on again.
Configure.CardPosted: Open Shop card posted in chat.

New.Hint: Pick what {name} sells and how wealthy the shop is. You can change all of it later.
New.Carries: {name} carries {count} items to sell. Open with its own items to sell only those.
New.Nothing: {name} carries nothing to sell yet. Stock and open rolls a shelf from the compendiums.

Configure.MenuHint: Trade, Show to players, Post Open Shop card and Stop being a shop are in this window's menu, at the top right.

Barter.Title: {merchant} and {customer}
Barter.TrayHint: Drag items here, or click them.
Barter.CannotCover: You don't have enough coins to cover it.

ConfirmWorn.Title: Trade worn gear?
ConfirmWorn.Body: {name} is equipped or attuned. Put it on offer anyway?

Barter.ToggleMode: Switch between Instant Trade and GM Approval

Attitude.Title: Attitude
Attitude.Hint: From -50 to 50. Players see only the face.

Tag.buyback: Buy back at the price you sold it for

Balance.CannotCover: Merchant can't cover this. Add goods to make up the gap.

Footer.CannotCover: The merchant can't pay that much in coins.

Status.countered: Countered. Sent back to the player.

Result.countered: The GM changed the offer. Check it and propose again.

Receipt.Title: Trade receipt
Receipt.RevertBody: Items and coins go back to where they were before the trade.

Ledger.Label: Ledger
Ledger.Hint: The last 50 trades here. Revert puts the items and coins back where they were.

Archetypes.Title: Shop archetypes
Archetypes.Hint: What each kind of shop stocks, which trade-ins it favors, and its haggling skills. Add your own or change the defaults.
Archetypes.Name: Name
Archetypes.FenceHint: Pays the Fence rate for every item, stolen goods included.
Archetypes.ToolsHint: Tool keys from dnd5e, separated by commas, such as smith, thief, alchemist or jeweler.
Archetypes.FilterHint: A list of filters. Each filter may have a type (weapon, equipment, consumable, tool, loot, container), subtypes, baseItems, and magical: true. An item matches if it fits any filter.
Archetypes.ReactionsHint: Optional. Situations: greeting, empty, short, even, generous. Bands: hostile, cold, neutral, warm, friendly. Anything left out uses the default lines.
Archetypes.ServicesHint: Optional. A list of services, priced in gold. Each has an id and a kind: identify, note or effect. Any can have a label, an icon and a note. A note can heal, such as "heal": "2d8+3". An effect can have a name, img, days, changes and statuses. Leave empty for the default services, or type [] for none.

identify.Name: Identify
identify.Hint: Learn what one of your unidentified items really is. It then sells at its true value.

removeCurse.Name: Remove Curse
removeCurse.Hint: Ends curses on you, so you can let go of a cursed item.

repair.Name: Repair
repair.Hint: Fixes a damaged weapon, armor or tool. Tell your GM which one.

roomAndMeal.Name: Room and meal
roomAndMeal.Hint: A warm meal and a bed for the night.

Kind.identify: Identifies one of your unidentified items.
Kind.note: The merchant does this for you, and the GM sees it in chat.
Kind.effect: Puts an effect on your character.

Service.NothingToIdentify: You have nothing unidentified, or it is already on offer.
Service.IdentifyOffered: Take {name} off the offer before you have it identified.

Stock.RestockConfirm: Roll a new shelf, keeping pinned items, and refill the purse?

Features.Title: Feature toggles
Features.Hint: Turn single features on or off on top of the complexity preset.
Features.Intro: Toggles start from the {mode} preset. Changes are kept for each complexity, so switching back finds them again.

purseLimit.Name: Merchant purse limit
purseLimit.Hint: Merchants can only pay with the coins they hold.

attitude.Name: Persistent attitude
attitude.Hint: Merchants remember how each customer treated them, and prices follow.

haggle.Name: Haggle checks
haggle.Hint: Customers can roll to push a price.

rolledInsight.Name: Rolled merchant checks
rolledInsight.Hint: The merchant rolls Insight against haggles and distractions, and Perception against thefts, instead of using passive scores.

appraisal.Name: Appraisal checks
appraisal.Hint: Unpriced loot is valued with a check. When off, it sells at a fixed scrap rate.

theft.Name: Theft attempts
theft.Hint: Customers can try to steal from a shop.

wanted.Name: Wanted board
wanted.Hint: Shops post items they pay extra for.

market.Name: Market modifiers
market.Hint: Temporary price rules for a scene or the whole world.

Haggle.Title: Haggle with {name}
Haggle.DcHint: Win and the discount applies to this trade. Lose and haggling is locked until tomorrow, and losing by 5 or more offends the merchant.
Haggle.OpposedHint: The merchant rolls Insight against you, so the DC stays hidden until the roll.
Haggle.LimitedHint: Limited Stock items allow at most 10% off.
Haggle.Off: Haggling is turned off in this world.
Haggle.Locked: {name} will not haggle with you again until tomorrow.
Haggle.Already: You already won a discount for this trade.
Haggle.BadAsk: That discount cannot be asked for.
Haggle.BadCheck: That check cannot be used to haggle here.
Haggle.NeedPurchase: Put something to buy on offer first.

Card.Opposed: The merchant's Insight sets DC {dc}. Rolled {total}.
Card.Failure: No deal. Haggling is locked until tomorrow.

Appraise.Title: Appraise {name}
Appraise.Hint: The merchant offers only scrap for {name}. Convince them it is worth more: DC {dc}. One try a day.
Appraise.Off: Appraisal checks are turned off in this world.
Appraise.NotScrap: That item already has a price.
Appraise.Tomorrow: The merchant will look at {name} again tomorrow.
Appraise.BadSkill: That check cannot be used to appraise.

Card.Ask: {customer} asks the merchant to look again at {item}, using {check}.
Card.Success: Appraised: the merchant pays a fair rate for it now.
Card.Failure: Not convinced. The merchant will look again tomorrow.

Result.Success: {name} appraised: the merchant pays a fair rate now.
Result.Failure: The merchant is not convinced about {name}. Try again tomorrow.

TrueValue.Title: True value: {name}
TrueValue.Label: True value
TrueValue.Hint: What a merchant pays on once this item is appraised. Leave empty to use its type's floor price.

Wanted.Title: Wanted
Wanted.Hint: This merchant pays extra for these. Bringing a named item also wins its favor.
Wanted.ConfigureHint: Rolled with each restock. Named items leave the board once someone brings one. The Open Shop card shows the board too.

hostile: I have nothing for the likes of you.
neutral: Good day. See anything you like?
warm: Ah, good to see you again!
Come in, come in. I kept a few things aside.
friendly: My favorite customer! What can I do for you?
There you are, friend. The kettle is on.

hostile: Well? I am not here to watch you stare.
cold: Take your time. Not too much of it.
neutral: Let me know when you have chosen.
Everything is for sale, for the right coin.
warm: Take all the time you need.
friendly: For you, I will see what I can do.

hostile: Is that an insult or a joke?
cold: That is well short. Try again.
I am not running a charity.
neutral: Not quite enough, I am afraid.
We are a little apart still.
warm: Close, but I have to eat too.
A bit more and we have a deal.
friendly: I would love to, but I cannot go that low.

warm: A good deal for us both.

hostile: More than fair. I will remember that.
Trying to buy my good will? It might work.
neutral: You will not hear me complain.

Ask.Title: Join the trade?
Ask.Body: {name} is already trading here. Join their trade and add your own items or coins?

Join.Title: Joining {lead} at {merchant}
Join.Heading: Joined trade
Join.Panel: Your items and coins go into {lead}'s offer at {merchant}.
Join.PanelHint: {lead} picks who gets the purchases and presses Accept for everyone.
Join.Ended: {name} left the shop, so the joined trade ended.
Join.Traded: {name} finished the trade with what you added.

PlayerTrade.Title: {first} and {second}
PlayerTrade.Heading: Trade between players
PlayerTrade.Rule: Both of you must accept. Any change to either offer resets both.

Market.Title: Shops
Market.Empty: Your party has not visited any merchants yet.
Market.EmptyGM: No shops yet. Select an NPC token on the map to set it up as a shop.

Rules.Title: Market rules
Rules.Hint: Temporary price changes for the whole world or one scene, such as war or a festival.
Rules.Intro: Each rule changes prices both ways for the goods it names, until its end date. Players see every rule in force under the balance.
Rules.Off: Market modifiers are off in this world, so these rules do nothing. Turn them on in Feature toggles.
Rules.Name: Name
Rules.CategoriesHint: Leave empty to change the price of every item.
Rules.PercentHint: Raise prices with a plus number, such as 30, or lower them with a minus number, such as -20.
Rules.DaysHint: In-game days from now. Leave empty to keep the rule until you remove it.
Rules.BadPercent: The price change must be a number other than 0, from -90 to 500.
Rules.BadCategory: That is not a kind of goods a rule can name.
Rules.BadDays: The length must be more than 0 days, or empty.

Market.ToolGM: Shops: set up, open and manage shops

Visit.TradedToday: Your last trade here was today.
Visit.TradedYesterday: Your last trade here was yesterday.
Visit.TradedDays: Your last trade here was {days} days ago.

Theft.Title: Theft
Theft.Confirm: You try to pocket one {item} without the merchant noticing. You won't know how hard it is, and getting caught has a price.
Theft.ConfirmDistracted: You try to pocket one {item} while {name} keeps the merchant busy. You roll with advantage, but getting caught still has a price.
Theft.Waiting: You wait for the right moment to take {item}. The GM decides if you get one.
Theft.Refused: No chance to take {item} comes up.
Theft.Answered: This theft has already been settled.
Theft.Recognized: {merchant} recognizes {item} as stolen and refuses the trade.
Theft.Ask: {customer} wants to pocket {item} from {merchant}. Allow the roll?

Result.fumble: Your hand slips, and {item} stays where it was.
Result.caught: The merchant catches you reaching for {item}.

Card.Distracted: Another character distracts the merchant, so the roll has advantage.
Card.taken: Taken. The merchant will notice at the next restock.
Card.fumble: Fumble. The item stays, and Suspicion is now {suspicion} until tomorrow.
Card.caught: Caught in the act. Choose what the merchant does.
Card.Distract: {name} tries to distract the merchant with {check}.
Card.DistractWorks: It works. The next theft attempt has advantage.
Card.Blamed: The merchant blames its last customer, {name}: attitude {value} on their next visit.
Card.Own: {merchant} knows {item} at once. {customer} is selling back what was stolen here.
Card.Looks: {customer} offers {item}, stolen from another merchant in this scene.
Card.NotRecognized: The merchant does not recognize it, and the trade goes on.
Card.Notoriety: {name} now has notoriety {points} in this scene.

Done.attitude: {merchant} will remember this. Attitude {value}, and {customer} is not welcome back today.
Done.guards: {merchant} shouts for the guards. {customer} has trouble coming.
Done.ban: {merchant} throws {customer} out for the rest of the day.

Distract.Title: Distract the merchant
Distract.Hint: Keep {merchant} busy so {lead} can try to steal with advantage. You roll against the merchant's Insight, once per attempt.
Distract.Success: The merchant is busy with you. The next theft attempt has advantage.
Distract.BadSkill: That check cannot be used to distract.
Distract.Tried: You already tried. Wait for the next theft attempt.

Theft.GuardHint: A guard makes theft harder at every shop in this scene.

Show.Title: Show {name} to players
Show.Hint: The shop opens on their screens for their own character, even if the shop is closed or they stand far away.

Identity.unique: One person: one shop on every map
Identity.generic: A kind of merchant: a shop per token

Hint.unique: Every token of {name} is the same shop, with the same stock, purse and memory of customers, on every map.
Hint.generic: Each token of {name} you place from now on becomes its own shop, starting as a copy of this one.
Hint.token: This token is its own shop, kept on the token only. Deleting the token deletes the shop. Choose One person to move this shop onto {name}, so it follows them to every map.
Hint.fresh: Each token rolls its own shelf and purse the first time someone trades there.

Fresh.Label: Roll new stock for each token
Fresh.Hint: Each token rolls its own shelf and purse the first time someone trades there.

Move.Title: Make this merchant one person?
Move.Body: {name} in the Actors sidebar takes this token's items, purse and shop records. Every token of {name} then shares this one shop, on every map.

Choose.Title: {name} is already a shop
Choose.Body: {name} already runs a shop through another token. Use that shop here too, and drop this token's own shelf? Or make this token a separate person with an actor of its own?

Identity.ChangeHint: One person keeps one shop on every map. A kind of merchant gives every token its own shop.
